Simulate longitudinal data with AR(1) within-subject errors

Source: R/simulate_ar1.r
ks_simulate_ar1.Rd

Generates a random sample of subjects with random intercepts and slopes, irregular observation times, and Gaussian AR(1) serially correlated residuals. The result is an groupedData object suitable for exploratory plots or simulation studies.

Usage

ks_simulate_ar1(
  n,
  beta0,
  beta1,
  ar.val = 0.4,
  sigma,
  tau0,
  tau1,
  tau01 = 0.3,
  m,
  seed = NULL
)

Arguments

n

Number of subjects (\(\ge 1\)).

beta0

Population mean intercept (fixed effect on the log-time scale).

beta1

Population mean slope (coefficient of \(\log(\mathrm{obs})\)).

ar.val

Autoregressive coefficient \(\phi\) for the within-subject errors (must lie strictly between \(-1\) and \(1\)).

sigma

Marginal standard deviation of the AR(1) error (after the scaling described in Details).

tau0, tau1

Standard deviations of random intercept and random slope.

tau01

Correlation between random intercept and slope (in \([-1,1]\)).

m

Maximum possible number of visits per subject (must be \(\ge 4\)). Each subject receives between 4 and m observations, always including time obs = 1.

seed

Optional integer; if not NULL, passed to set.seed before random draws (reproducibility).

Value

An groupedData object (also inherits from data.frame) with columns id, obs, and y.

Details

Observation counts \(p_i\) are uniform on \(\{4,\ldots,m\}\) (rounded from continuous uniforms). Observation times are \(1\) plus a random subset of \(\{2,\ldots,m\}\) of size \(p_i-1\).

Random effects \((b_{0i}, b_{1i})'\) are bivariate normal with mean zero, SDs tau0, tau1 and correlation tau01. Outcomes are $$y_{ij} = (\beta_0 + b_{0i}) + (\beta_1 + b_{1i})\log(t_{ij}) + \varepsilon_{ij}$$ with \(\varepsilon_{i\cdot}\) an AR(1) Gaussian series. Innovations are scaled so that the marginal residual SD is sigma: arima.sim(...) is multiplied by \(\sigma\sqrt{1-\phi^2}\).

See also

arima.sim, mvrnorm, groupedData

Examples

set.seed(1)
dt <- ks_simulate_ar1(
  n = 10, beta0 = 5, beta1 = 1, ar.val = 0.4, sigma = 2,
  tau0 = 1, tau1 = 0.5, tau01 = 0.2, m = 8, seed = 1L
)
head(dt)
#> Grouped Data: y ~ obs | id
#> <environment: 0x76e49313f0>
#>   id obs        y
#> 1  1   1 5.193845
#> 2  1   2 3.111578
#> 3  1   4 5.768827
#> 4  1   6 6.680145
#> 5  1   8 6.771501
#> 6  2   1 2.254783
